document_meta.title: Ohio Forest Action Plan (Forest Resource Assessment and Strategy)

orientation.summary: The 2020 Ohio Forest Action Plan (OFAP) is a combined Forest Resource Assessment and Forest Resource Strategy produced by the Ohio Department of Natural Resources (ODNR) Division of Forestry, required under the 2008 Farm Bill. It is a comprehensive statewide forest resource document covering biological diversity, productive capacity, ecosystem health, soil and water, carbon cycles, socioeconomic benefits, and legal frameworks. The document engages substantively with climate change as a current and future threat to Ohio's forests, referencing warming trends, altered precipitation, and projected shifts in species ranges and hardiness zones. Range shifts are addressed primarily through the lens of tree species distribution modeling (Climate Change Tree Atlas, RCP scenarios applied to Ohio quadrants), with explicit discussion of assisted migration as a management option. The document performs its own geospatial analysis for priority areas and incorporates results from external vulnerability assessments and species distribution models; it references but does not independently develop climate models.

projects: Central Appalachians Forest Ecosystem Vulnerability Assessment (Butler et al. 2015): Applied to Ohio, West Virginia, and Maryland forest ecosystems. Assessed vulnerability of nine forest ecosystem types, providing ratings (low/moderate/high) that directly inform management planning. Results are incorporated into Ohio's strategy for identifying resilient vs. vulnerable forest types.

Climate Change Tree Atlas (Iverson et al. 2019c / Prasad et al. 2014): Applied to four 1x1° blocks covering Ohio. Modeled future habitat suitability for 66–81 tree species under RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5, providing evidence of which species are likely to gain or lose habitat and which are candidates for assisted migration. Results directly inform tree species management recommendations.

Hobey Hollow Climate Adaptation Planning (2015, Shawnee State Forest): ODNR worked with NIACS to assess site-specific climate impacts and identify adaptation actions for a 243-acre demonstration area, providing a proof-of-concept for integrating vulnerability assessment into local forest management.
